(6 actions) The trap loses 1 action per disabled or destroyed sluice. On each of its actions, the water rushing from the sluices flows through the room, creating a river of churning water that fills the room to several inches and makes the floor of the chamber into difficult terrain. The water level never rises above this level in the room, as it drains out of the chutes to the south and begins to flood the quarry pit (area J2). On the trap's second turn, the water starts filling the four slave pits in area J2. Each of the trap's actions fills the pits 4 inches (2 feet per round if all sluices are functional). If the slave pits fill to their total depth of 12 feet and the grates over the slave pits aren't open, the slaves begin to drown, dying if they aren't freed in 5 rounds. Once the slave pits are full, the water continues to slowly fill the central area over the course of an hour until it empties the reservoir and floods area J2 to a depth of 15 feet.

Other options beyond disabling or destroying the sluices could prevent the flooding of the quarry pit at your discretion.

details.routine: If Gerhard lights the black powder fuse, it burns at a speed of 10 feet each round; when the fuse reaches a keg 6 rounds later, the black powder bomb explodes. The bomb explodes immediately if he shoots a barrel with his blunderbuss.
details.disable:
No special skills are required to disable this manually activated trap. As an Interact action, a PC can sweep aside some black powder to interrupt the fuse line, but this doesn't prevent Gerhard from activating a keg via blunderbuss. A keg that is removed from its position (either by being thrown over the cliff or merely carried away) retains its explosive potential, but as long as one of the three kegs are removed they no longer have the precise placement required to trigger a collapse-an explosion at this point merely inflicts fire damage in the appropriate areas but does not particularly damage the temple structure itself.

A keg's contents can be dispersed by scattering the gunpowder to the wind (most efficiently by pouring it over the cliff side) as a 2-action activity, or rendered permanently inert by pouring a gallon of water into the powder, inhibiting its explosive qualities. The kegs themselves can be destroyed with damage (note that the AC listed below for each keg takes into account the fact that Gerhard has wedged the kegs into nooks in the temple's stone flooring and walls), but note that any fire damage (including incidental fire damage from area effects like a fireball or Gerhard's blunderbuss) causes them to explode. At your option, other actions may be similarly effective at disabling this hazard.

details.routine:
On its turn, the fire spreads into a number of additional squares equal to half the number of squares the fire currently occupies, with a minimum of 1 square. You determine the squares the fire spreads into-typically those with the most flammable materials. Any creature that ends its turn next to the flames takes @Damage[1d6[fire]] damage, and any creature within the flames takes @Damage[4d6[fire]] damage. Both of these have a @Check[reflex|dc:17|basic|traits:complex,environmental,fire,hazard] save. A creature can take damage from flames only once per round. (For simplicity, track damage only for the NPCs and their allies, not for the spectators; Turn 5 and Turn 7 have instructions regarding the spectators' health).

The fire has an additional effect on each of its turns after the first.

Turn 2 The chamber's northern door flies open and flames burst through, igniting the @Template[square|distance:10]{10-foot-by-10-foot area} in front of the door. All fires spread on subsequent turns, at the same rate listed above. Any fires that join together become one fire for this purpose.

Turn 4+ Creatures in the room take @Damage[1d6[untyped]] damage from smoke inhalation at the ends of their turns. Anyone who uses an Interact action to tie a wet rag around their nose and mouth (or uses another creative solution) halves the damage.

Turn 5 Spectators still inside the room fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} from burns and smoke inhalation.

Turn 7 Spectators still in the room die.
details.disable:
Eliminating the hazard requires dousing the flames. Water typically clears a 5-foot square if the amount is small (such as that from @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WzLKjSw6hsBhuklC]{Create Water} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.jfVCuOpzC6mUrf6f]{Hydraulic Push}). Larger amounts of water, such as a full bucket, typically douse a @Template[square|distance:10]{10-foot-by-10-foot area} (or 4 squares in some other shape). Throwing a bucket of water on flames requires an Interact action. A waterskin doesn't contain enough water to put out even 1 square of fire. Cold can also put out fire, but only if the cold can affect an area; cold is usually less effective than water, so a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.EpxmUtLpCkE8R6KJ]{Frost Vial} typically puts out 1 square of fire, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gYjPm7YwGtEa1oxh]{Ray of Frost} is ineffective.

Fountain Circle, located outside town hall, has several working water pumps. These are far enough away that it's impractical for a PC to bring water back and forth. However, a PC might instruct the more steely nerved spectators to create a bucket brigade. It takes 15 spectators (which can include those rescued by councilors as well as by PCs) to set this up, and 2 rounds for the townspeople to line up and begin pumping water from Fountain Circle. As of the 3rd round, there is a bucket of water available for the PCs to use at the chamber's southern entrance at the beginning of each PC's turn. Members of a bucket brigade are lined up outside the chamber, and don't take damage from smoke inhalation.

If a PC does want to carry the water, it's 150 feet from the chamber's southern door to a pump, so it 6 actions are usually needed to reach the pumps or return. Filling a bucket requires an Interact action.

Other methods might also help control the fire, as you determine. For example, the PCs might be able to find something to barricade the fire with to control its path, or use a cloak to beat out some of the fire.

Success The creature is entangled, and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} until the end of the looms' next turn.

Failure The creature is tangled in the yarn and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} until the end of the loom's next turn—or if it already has the clumsy condition, it becomes restrained (see critical failure).

details.routine:
(1 action) The mirror absorbs another reflected creature into the mirror (@Check[reflex|dc:42]) and replaces it with a mirror duplicate. Mirror duplicates act on their own initiative, using the same statistics as the original creature, but with an evil alignment (changing only abilities that shift with the alignment change).

Mirror duplicates are legendary in Intimidation and are permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened}, but they can use this additional action only to Demoralize.

A mirror duplicate can spend 3 actions in contact with the mirror to return to its original dimension and release the creature it duplicated, but most mirror duplicates prefer not to.

details.reset: The mirror is always ready to absorb creatures into another dimension. 10 minutes after a creature is sucked into the mirror, if an ally doesn't rescue the creature using the Thievery skill, the creature reaches the mirror dimension, where it could be captured or killed. In the mirror dimension, it counts as a mirror duplicate, so the denizens of the other dimension can't destroy the mirror on their side while the absorbed creature is there. These dimensions are alternate realities, not planes, so even rituals like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.5bTt2CvYHPvaR7QQ]{Interplanar Teleport} can't reach them.

(12 actions) The trap loses 1 action for each of its 12 ceiling trapdoors that are disabled. On each of the trap's actions, it pours water into the room, filling it to a depth of one inch. If one of the portcullises is breached, the trap fills the room at half the rate, and if both are breached, it fills at one quarter the rate. Once the cascade of water begins, it's easy enough for a PC to avoid the downpour, but any creature that deliberately enters the cascade is subjected to the trap's Rushing Water reaction. If a creature is struck by Rushing Water while already underwater, the result of its Reflex save is automatically improved one degree of success.

The flooding ends and the trap deactivates once the area is filled to the ceiling-at this point, the water's surface is at the level of the river, and at the top of the stairs leading down from areas D4 and D6. A Medium or smaller creature can try to Swim to freedom through one of the 5-foot-wide tunnels leading to the river from a trapdoor, but doing so requires navigating 200 feet of flooded tunnels.

(3 actions) Up to four different creatures in area A12 are each targeted by one of the floating, churning spheres of wine drifting through the air; it hurtles toward them and douses them with wine that turns to life- draining blood as it strikes unerringly. The haunt cannot target the same creature more than once each round. After the haunt is reduced to its broken threshold of 53 HP, it can target no more than two different creatures. A creature targeted by the lights of the lost must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:37|traits:damaging-effect] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes @Damage[4d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} from drunkenness.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[8d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.

Critical Failure The takes @Damage[16d6[void]] damage, is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3}, and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}. As long as the creature is doomed from this trap, they cannot reduce their sickened condition below 1, and they take a -1 circumstance penalty on all further saving throws made against fear effects as lingering traces of the terror the priests felt loom in their memories.

details.routine:
(4 actions) If the PCs successfully sought shelter with a Survival check, the storm takes no actions if the GM fails a @Check[flat|dc:16]. Otherwise, the storm takes four of the following actions, each determined by rolling a [[/gmr 1d4]], during the round. On each successive round, the number of actions the storm takes is reduced by 1; when the storm is reduced to 0 actions in this way, the hazard ends.

  • 1 Thunderclap A blast of sound rips through the region. Unsheltered armies must attempt a DC 30 Morale check or increase their shaken value by 1. Unsheltered PCs take @Damage[10d6[sonic]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:38|basic]).
  • 2 Lightning The tempest takes its Raging Storm reaction as a single action.
  • 3 Tornado A tornado funnel extends down from the storm to unerringly strike at a PC, who must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:38] save.

Critical Success The PC escapes unscathed.

Success The PC is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} and takes @Damage[8d6[bludgeoning]] damage.

Failure The PC is hurled through the air, taking @Damage[8d6[bludgeoning]] damage and then falling 1d6×10 feet for appropriate falling damage, landing prone.

Critical Failure As failure, but @Damage[8d6[bludgeoning]] damage and a fall of [[/r 10*(2d8) #Feet Fallen]]{2d8 x 10 feet}.

  • 4 Renewal Blasts of wind tear through the area but do no real damage. Attempt a @Check[flat|dc:11]; on a success, the number of actions the storm takes next round is not reduced as usual.

details.routine: The GM rolls a @Check[flat|dc:9|showDC:owner] to determine if the building partially collapses, increasing the DC as listed above. On a critical success, the effect is the same, but the debris deals @Damage[12d6[bludgeoning]] damage to [[/r 2d4 #Targets]] randomly chosen targets instead (@Check[reflex|dc:35|basic|name:Falling Debris|traits:hazard,complex,environmental,kaiju] save; on a critical failure, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by rubble until freed [[[/act force-open dc=38]], [[/act escape dc=35]]]).

details.routine: (1 action) On its initiative, the whorl pulls down any creature within it that can cast spells or that is wielding a magic item. A creature submerged to the waist becomes submerged to the neck, and a creature submerged to the neck is pulled under and must hold its breath to avoid suffocation. If a creature has no spells or magic items, the mana whorl is merely difficult terrain. A creature caught in a mana whorl can attempt a @Check[athletics|dc:23] check to Swim to either raise itself by one step if submerged to the neck or worse, or to move 5 feet if submerged only to the waist. On a critical failure, the creature is pulled down by one step. A creature that Swims out of the whorl escapes the hazard and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} in a space adjacent to the whorl. Other creatures can Aid the creature, typically by using a rope or similar aid, or attempt to pull the creature out with their own @Check[athletics|dc:23] check, with the same results as if the creature attempted the check. If a creature has only magic items and no ability to cast spells, dropping all the items releases that creature, and it can move through the mana whorl as normal difficult terrain.

Spellcasters and magic items fed to the whorl are devoured whole.
details.reset: The hazard continues to suck in anyone with magic until it is satiated (see Disable above). Magpies leave any satiated whorls.

details.routine:
The rift pulls creatures within 500 feet toward it. The rift can pull any creature, regardless of its size. Creatures in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:45|name:Planar Rift|traits:complex,conjuration,divine,environmental,kaiju,teleportation,hazard] or @Check[reflex|dc:45|name:Planar Rift|traits:complex,conjuration,divine,environmental,kaiju,teleportation,hazard] save (the creature's choice) to resist the effects of this pull or attempt to grab something to avoid getting pulled.

Critical Success The creature resists the pull and doesn't move toward the rift.

Success The creature is moved 25 feet toward the rift.

Failure The creature is moved 50 feet toward the rift.

Critical Failure The creature is moved 100 feet toward the rift. The harsh pull causes the creature to take @Damage[10d6[bludgeoning]] damage.

If a creature is directly beneath the rift when the rift pulls it, the creature instead attempts a @Check[fortitude|dc:50|name:Pull Into the Rift|traits:complex,conjuration,divine,environmental,kaiju,teleportation,hazard] or @Check[reflex|dc:50|name:Pull Into the Rift|traits:complex,conjuration,divine,environmental,kaiju,teleportation,hazard] save (the creature's choice) to avoid being pulled into the rift. On a failure, the creature is pulled up into the rift and thrown to a random point on the plane on the other side.

details.routine:
Each turn, the walls use 1 action. Roll a [[/gmr 1d10 #Routine Result]]{d10} and look up the result on the following list to determine which action the walls uses that round.

1–4 Single Target The walls lash out at a random hero in the room. Roll a [[/gmr 1d4 #Random Hero]]{d4} and count to the number you rolled, starting with the player on your left, to determine which hero gets attacked. The shadow lash is a ranged Strike with +10 to hit. On a hit, it deals @Damage[2d6[void]] damage (doubled on a critical hit as normal).

5–7 Wall Barrage The shadow arms lunge out from their respective wall, assaulting any one near an active wall. This hits any creature within 10 feet of an active wall (within 10 feet of a shadow hand on the map), dealing @Damage[2d6[void]|options:area-damage] damage. Each hero must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:15|basic|options:area-effect] save, taking no damage on a critical success, half damage on a success, full damage on a failure, and double damage on a critical failure.

8–9 Split Assault The shadows lash out against one half of the room. Roll [[/gmr 1d20 #Even Western Half, Odd Eastern Half]]{any die}. If the result is even, they assault the western half; otherwise, they assault the eastern half. This deals @Damage[2d6[void]|options:area-damage] damage to each creature in that half of the room, and each hero must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:15|basic|options:area-effect] save.

10 Overwhelming Assault Like the split assault attack, but it targets everyone in the room.

A hero must succeed at a @Check[thievery|dc:18|traits:hazard|name:Prevent Blocks from Falling] check on the triggering square or the ceiling to prevent the stone blocks from falling.

details.routine:
Each turn, the fountain uses 1 action. Roll a [[/gmr 1d10]] and look up the result on the following list to determine which action it uses that round.

  • 1-4 Single Target The statue spins about and sprays water at a single random target in the room. Roll a [[/gmr 1d4]] and count to the number you rolled, starting with the player on your left, to determine which hero gets attacked. The spray is a ranged Strike.
  • 5-7 Corner Spray The statue spins about, firing a spray of water at each corner of the room that still has a functioning corner mechanism. A non-participant can step in front of a participant as a reaction. This blocks the damage from the ritual caster, but the non-participant must then attempt the Fortitude save.

In addition to dealing damage, the ritual's surge of energy brings a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pfs-season-1-bestiary.Actor.mjW1q98gMnEmZJKt]{Shadow Wisp} into the room. Wisps act at the end of the ritual's turn. If there are already two shadow wisps in the room, instead of creating a new wisp, the ritual restores @Damage[10[healing]] Hit Points to each wisp.
details.disable:
Seven flaws have appeared in the ritual circle, dancing like shadowy flames. Each of Tavvar's three aides keeps one flaw under control as long as they are alive, while Tavvar herself staves off the ritual's implosion as listed in the ritual anchor ability below.

Each flaw can be repaired with a successful @Check[occultism|dc:22] or DC 18 (trained) check using a skill related to the flaw's original cause (see the table below). Regardless of success or failure, a PC who attempts an Occultism check to disable the hazard learns the cause of the flaws and the skills that can be used to overcome it.

Each success on a check to repair a flaw using these other skills reduces the DC of the Occultism check to repair a flaw by 2. Instead of using skill checks, the PCs can use force to stabilize the ritual. A PC who defeats a shadow wisp automatically repairs one flaw.

d4 Cause of Flaw Skills to Overcome
1 Harried (a "publish or perish" culture at the College of Mystery led to Tavvar cutting corners in the ritual's execution, so some runes aren't drawn quite right) @Check[arcana|dc:18] (trained) or @Check[thievery|dc:18] (trained)
2 Misplaced Affection (Tavvar is from Nidal and subconsciously hopes the ritual will show that there is some good in her homeland; she included some Shadowtongue in the runes and it's enhancing the energy @Check[society|dc:18] (trained) or @Check[religion|dc:18] (trained)

details.routine:
(4 actions) The burning spirits shriek and howl, swooping in and out of the forges to the south, which roar into scorching life. The spirits scoop up gobs of phantasmal molten dawnsilver and hurl them at different targets in the room. Up to four randomly determined creatures are targeted in this way with molten dawnsilver Strikes (the spirits can target any creature in area B5). A single creature may be targeted only once per round, so if there are fewer than four different targets, the haunt's extra actions are lost. The haunt also loses two actions from its routine if one of the two forges are destroyed.

On a critical hit from a molten dawnsilver Strike, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round as the molten dawnsilver swiftly cools and encases the target. Molten dawnsilver produced by the haunt vanishes entirely 1 round after it's been thrown.
details.disable: @Check[religion|dc:38] (master) to exorcise the spirits or @Check[intimidation|dc:41] to quell them with furious anger; three total successes are required to disable the haunt
details.reset: 1 hour.

details.routine: (4 actions) The hazard uses Steal Magic twice. Once the implements of at least three runelord statues are charged, the hazard uses its next available action to Transfer Magic. If the hazard starts its turn with the Belimarius statue charged, the hazard uses its reaction to Empower Barrier. A disabled runelord statue can't use Steal Magic. If the Belimarius statue is disabled, the hazard can't use Transfer Magic or Empower Barrier.
details.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:45] (master) to unweave the magic surrounding a statue, @Check[athletics|dc:48] (expert) to wrest a statue's implement from its hands, @Check[thievery|dc:48] (expert) to slip an implement free, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the magic that empowers the statue. Increase the DCs to disable the Belimarius statue by 2. Each statue must be disabled or counteracted separately, and disabling the Belimarius statue or all nine other statues permanently disables the hazard.
details.reset: The hazard resets automatically if not disabled.

details.routine:
(1+ hours, @Check[flat|dc:18]) Rifts detonate with raw planar essence. As the hazard progresses, the ruptures grow more frequent until they merge together into a gaping portal (this final stage might be prevented with good fortune or successful efforts to Prepare). Ruptures occur once per 10 minutes for the first hour and once per minute for the second hour. The frequency with which each unprepared creature in the area is hit by a rupture depends upon their proximity to the hazard's epicenter. If the hazard proceeds into a third hour, all creatures and objects in the area take the hazard's damage one final time before being swallowed up by the burgeoning portal and deposited on the other plane.

(1+ minutes, @Check[flat|dc:17]) Small asteroids rain down across the sky, battering and incinerating those caught in their path before carving craters. Over the course of a minute, enough asteroids smash into the ground and explode to inflict @Damage[7d10[bludgeoning],14d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage to any unprepared characters in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:46|basic] save). The @Template[type:burst|distance:40]{40-foot-radius} craters left behind are greater difficult terrain.

The material raining down from outer space includes chunks of adamantine. Adamantine's ability to break through the Hardness of materials is particularly lethal at terminal velocity. The falling adamantine has Hardness 20, allowing the asteroid's bludgeoning damage to overcome the Hardness of all materials with less Hardness, including shelters that would otherwise provide cover. Cover that's destroyed by the bludgeoning damage provides no protection against the fire damage.

(5 actions) On its initiative, the malfunctioning perfumery takes the following five actions, in order. For each success at disabling it, the hazard loses one action. The targets for actions 2–5 are randomly chosen from creatures in the room, with no one creature being targeted more than once before all other creatures in the room have been targeted. For example, a party of 4 PCs will each be targeted by one of these actions. If just a single PC is in the room, they will be targeted by all four.

  • 1: Crushing Notes 1 (olfactory, poison) The malfunctioning machinery exudes a blast of concentrated and overwhelming perfume notes into area B11. Creatures in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:45|options:inflicts:stunned|traits:olfactory,poison] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} on a critical failure).

  • 2: Nozzle Spray 1 (poison) Nozzles built into the machinery extend out to spray toxic, overwhelmingly cloying perfume in multiple directions. One randomly determined target in area B11 takes @Damage[14d6[poison]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:45|basic|traits:poison] save).

  • 3: Sillage 1 (emotion, mental) A larger, more intimidating nozzle than the one utilized in the previous action extends forward and violently sprays a staggering array of different scents at a random target in the room. The overwhelming mixture of lingering scent (the perfume's sillage) causes the creature to take @Damage[10d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:45|basic|options:inflicts:slowed|traits:emotion,mental] save); on a failed save, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round by the overwhelming scents.

  • 4: Oil Spill 1 (fire) Sparks from grinding machinery ignite a patch of spilled oil somewhere in the room—a random creature in area B11 takes @Damage[10d6[fire],4d6[persistent,fire]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:45|basic|traits:fire] save).

  • 5: Boiling Beaker 1 (emotion, mental) A pressurized beaker containing boiling fluids springs a leak, and a dislodged tube sprays disorienting, psychotropic fumes at a random creature in the room, who must then succeed at a @Check[will|dc:44|options:inflicts:confused|traits:emotion,mental] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure).

details.routine:
(10+ minutes, @Check[flat|dc:15]) The colossus rampage affects the entire area, but whether or not the affected area remains static, moves, expands, or otherwise changes is left to you to determine as the story needs. At the start of each minute, unprepared creatures in the area take @Damage[(3d10+10)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:47|basic] save). A creature that fails the save is jostled enough that they're @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for that minute, while a creature that critically fails is pinned under fallen debris and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} until they [[/act escape dc=47]].

Two additional effects, based on the nature of the creatures and the battlefield, take place during that minute. Roll [[/gmr 1d10]] for each to determine on which round during that minute each effect takes place (rerolling duplicate rounds). You can create alternative abilities to better fit the nature of the creatures in the stampede, but in general, consider selecting one ability that imposes a condition or battlefield effect and one that deals damage. Note that these effects can affect prepared and unprepared creatures in the area, but when a prepared creature attempts a save against any of these effects, they increase their result by one degree of success.

(3 actions) When the shattered runewell takes its first action, a towering, 30-foot-tall image of Runelord Xanderghul formed from scintillating magenta and violet light and fire looms up from the runewell. On each of the hazard's three actions, this manifestation of Runelord Xanderghul scowls down at the PCs, and tendrils of strangely colored fire lash out of the runewell, each targeting a different PC in the area. The effects of these tendrils vary according to their color; these ranged Strikes can target anyone in the Eye of Arrogance and accrue multiple attack penalties normally.
details.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:37] (master) or @Check[occultism|dc:40] (master) to redirect the magic back in on itself and cancel out the danger, or @Check[crafting|dc:40] (legendary) to reposition runewell fragments so they're not dangerous; three total successes are required to disable the shattered runewell

details.routine: (6 actions) Each Rune Sentry grants the hazard 1 action; a Rune Sentry that's plummeted or been disabled or destroyed reduces the hazard's available actions by 1. On the hazard's turn, all active Rune Sentries spend their action to use Lightning Arc.
details.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:45] (legendary) to turn the lightning back against the sentry, causing the head to plummet, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract the magic that empowers the sentry, causing it to plummet. Each sentry must be counteracted or destroyed separately.

details.routine: (4 actions) The haunt uses Vomit Maggot three times, then Poisonous Belch once. For each success at Disabling the haunt, the haunt loses one Vomit Maggot action. Destroying a mask also removes one of the haunt's Vomit Maggot actions. Once the haunt can no longer use Vomit Maggot, it immediately regains three actions and replaces Vomit Maggot with Spectral Scythe. Destroying a scythe also removes one of the haunt's Spectral Scythe actions. Once the haunt loses all three of its Spectral Scythe actions, the haunt is destroyed.
details.disable: @Check[occultism|dc:45] (legendary) or Religion (legendary) to exorcise Zutha's spirit, or @Check[intimidation|dc:48] (master) or @Check[performance|dc:48] (master) to recite the details of Zutha's defeat; six total successes are required to disable the haunt.
details.reset: The haunt deactivates once no living creatures remain nearby. The haunt resets 1 hour later.

details.disable: @Check[athletics|dc:48] (legendary) to grab one of the comet's tails and rip it free; @Check[occultism|dc:45] or @Check[religion|dc:45] (master) to exorcise the divine energy of the red tail (which is infused with Gorum's legacy) or the black tail (infused with the nihilism of Abaddon's Eclipse); @Check[arcana|dc:45] (master) to unweave the magic of the rainbow tail (Xanderghul's mythic power); or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract one of the tails. Each tail must be disabled separately to disable the hazard.
details.reset:
(1 action) The Trinity Star flies at a speed of 60 feet, moving through the spaces of as many creatures as possible. Each creature the Trinity Star moves through must make a @Check[reflex|dc:42] save with the following results.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes @Damage[6d6[force]] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[11d6[force]] damage and is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Critical Failure The creature takes @Damage[22d6[force]] damage, is knocked prone, and if the creature is mythic, they lose 1 Mythic Point. If the Trinity Star has lost any of its tails, it regrows one of them (chosen at random if it's lost two tails).

details.routine:
(5+ minutes, @Check[flat|dc:18]) The megatsunami's wave overtakes and crushes everything in its path. It rips buildings off their foundations and tears up trees by their roots. Prepared creatures have managed to reach an area of high ground or another form of safety, but unprepared creatures in the area are caught up in the flood and battered by a combination of water and debris.

Unprepared creatures take @Damage[(5d12+30)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:43|basic] save) when the megatsunami hits and are thereafter surrounded by water. If they can't breathe water, they must hold their breath or begin to drown. Each round, a creature can attempt a @Check[athletics|dc:40] check to Swim up near the surface or to keep their head above water for the remainder of the minute once they reach the surface.

At the start of the next four minutes, the megatsunami has carried each unprepared character 250 feet inland. At this time, each unprepared character takes @Damage[(3d12+20)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:40|basic] save). A character who managed that minute to remain near the surface gains a result one degree of success better than their actual rolled result, with a critical success indicating they've managed to clamber out of the surge onto high ground and are now prepared.

At the end of the five minutes, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:18] to determine if a new wave repeats the routine. Characters already swept inland only become affected by these following waves once the rushing water reaches them, but until then they can Swim in the choppy floodwaters with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:30] check, potentially reaching safety or high ground before the next wave hits. Once a region is flooded by a megatsunami, it typically remains flooded for several hours.

details.routine:
(2 actions) On the trap's first action, it attempts a water jet ranged Strike on all creatures outside of the water in this room or on the stairs leading up to area A5. On its second action, the primal magic infusing the waters attempts to seep into the minds of those within it, forcing each creature in the water to attempt a @Check[will|dc:39|options:area-effect,damaging-effect,inflicts:stupefied] save against the following effects.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected

Success The creature takes @Damage[4d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[8d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 24 hours. While the creature is stupefied, it takes an additional –2 status penalty to checks made to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}.

Critical Failure As failure, but @Damage[16d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3}, and the stupefied condition has an unlimited duration.

(3 actions) On her initiative each round, Sorshen can spend her three actions on any of the following options, following PC suggestions if requested. She cannot use any action from the following list more than once per round.

Aid Ally 1 Sorshen uses her magic to empower one of the PCs, granting that PC a +4 circumstance bonus to attack rolls until the start of her next turn. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.MNITD4PrcyRCqPbK]{Effect: Queen Sorshen's Aid (Aid Ally)}

Dispel Pride 1 Sorshen attempts to counteract a magic effect put in place by Xanderghul, with a counteract rank of 9th and a [[/gmr 1d20+40 #Counteract]]{+40} modifier for the roll.

Distracting Presence 1 Sorshen uses her power to distract Xanderghul, causing him to lose his resistance to mental damage until the start of her next turn and also to attempt a @Check[will|dc:50] save with the following results.

Critical Success Xanderghul takes no further penalty, and is temporarily immune to Distracting Presence for 24 hours.

Success Xanderghul is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of his turn.

Failure Xanderghul is off-guard until the start of Sorshen's next turn.

Critical Failure As failure, but Xanderghul is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} as long as he remains off-guard.

Indulgent Arcana 1 Sorshen empowers a PC's magic, so that the next spell with the mental trait they cast before Sorshen's next turn increases its save DC and attack roll by 2 and removes the spell's incapacitation trait, if any. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.KFmJLxZAFQ2Q7C1N]{Effect: Queen Sorshen's Aid (Indulgent Arcana)}

Sinuous Strike 1 Sorshen swings her guisarme, usurping some of Xanderghul's own power to manifest an illusory duplicate that attempts a guisarme Strike against him.

Each creature in the hazard's area takes @Damage[6d12[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:42|basic|traits:arcane,emotion,illusion,mental] save). On a failed save, a creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 2} on a critical failure). A PC reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage is shunted back into area C7.

A creature that takes damage while Climbing the webs must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] save or fall. A creature can try to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.3yoajuKjwHZ9ApUY]{Grab an Edge} (@Check[reflex|dc:40]). On a success, they lose one success they've earned to escape the hazard but otherwise arrest their fall. On a failure, they plummet into the void, losing all Athletics successes they've earned to escape the hazard. Each round on their turn, the character can try to Grab an Edge again, but each time they fail to do so, the party must earn an additional success to escape the hazard. Characters who fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} or repeatedly fail to Grab an Edge might effectively become lost in the void, though once the nightmare hazard is disabled, they appear along with the rest of the PCs in Liralarue's Prison.
details.disable: @Check[acrobatics|dc:47] to Fly through the space without becoming stuck in the webs, @Check[athletics|dc:50] to Climb the webs and make progress forward through the infinite, @Check[nature|dc:47] or @Check[occultism|dc:47] or @Check[arcana|dc:50] or @Check[religion|dc:50] (legendary) to collapse the extradimensional space, or @Check[perception|dc:52] to peer through the visions of Golarion to notice discrepancies that help keep the overwhelming despair from setting in; six successes disables the hazard, causing it to vanish forever and shunting all creatures to Liralarue's Prison.
details.reset: The hazard resets automatically once no creatures are in the area.

details.routine:
A Voyage Through the Infinite (1 action) Every round on its turn, the trap inflicts all creatures in the shaft with the perception that they have been hurtling at an unimaginable speed through the vastness of space. The stars are so distant that no indication of movement can be observed or felt beyond that overwhelming mental conviction. At the same time, the creatures feel as if something unimaginably powerful and hungry is chasing them... and gaining on them. Any PC who looks over their shoulder sees that the stars are indeed winking out behind them, as if an immense black object were growing closer or as if the stars themselves were vanishing. While the PC's body is somehow protected by the vastness of space, their minds are not—each PC must attempt a @Check[will|dc:40] save.

Critical Success As success below, but the creature also realizes they're reliving the memories of Runelord Xanderghul—like him, they're escaping some sort of horrific fate and are hurtling toward Golarion. The next time this creature achieves a critical success against this trap, they suddenly see Golarion loom large, and as they witness their "crash" into the Throne of the Troll King, they suddenly wake, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}, in area C1 at the heart Xin-Cyrusian. If any other PCs are still trapped in the Falling Star's Memories, a PC in Xin-Cyrusian knows instinctively that they can call out to those trapped PCs—each PC in Xin-Cyrusian who does so reduces the save DC against A Voyage Through the Infinite for those still trapped by 5.

Success The creature realizes they're experiencing the path the Trinity Star took through the cosmos and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature's grip on reality fades as they experience what seems like years or even decades of hurtling adrift through a vast expanse. The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 24 hours or increases the value of their stupefied condition by 1 if they're already stupefied.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} (or increase the stupefied condition by 2).

Special If this trap would cause a creature's stupefied condition to exceed @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 5}, the creature instead "crashes" to the ground on the hilltop outside, about ten feet from the Throne of the Troll King. The creature takes @Damage[10d6[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:40|basic] save), and their stupefied condition now has an unlimited duration.
details.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:40] (master) to unweave the magic left in the wake of the Trinity Star's passage, @Check[thievery|dc:43] (expert) to etch temporary runes to siphon away the magic, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (8th rank; counteract DC 33) to counteract the magic; three successes are required to disable the trap. Once the PCs are within the trap's overwhelming illusion, they can still attempt these checks to disable it, but the check DCs increase by 2.
details.reset: The trap resets automatically.

details.routine:
(6 actions) On its turn, the Mirror of Glory targets random PCs in the area with distortions of their reality, spending an action to target one PC. If it has actions remaining after targeting the PCs, it spends any remaining actions repairing damage done to itself at the rate of 25 HP restored per action spent. If the mirror hasn't been damaged, then these unused actions are lost. Each time the Mirror of Glory targets a PC with a distortion, roll 1d6 and consult the entries below to determine what the PC experiences and any subsequent effects. The trap loses one action for each successful check made to disable it, but this doesn't reduce the number of distortions it's capable of creating. When a PC experiences a distortion, they take @Damage[10d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:37|basic] save), but on a failed saving throw, the PC suffers that distortion's additional effect.

1—Beauty: The PC regards Xanderghul as the most attractive figure they've ever seen. Additional effect: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round.

2—Cruelty: The PC sees Xanderghul as a demonic figure capable of unimaginable cruelty, who lashes out at the PC with dozens of blades and poisoned needles meant to carve away their strength. Additional effect: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 24 hours.

3—Disappointment: To the PC, Xanderghul suddenly seems to be an intimidating parental figure, commanding officer, or other person with authority whose disapproval induces tremors of nervousness. Additional effect: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 24 hours.

4—Jealousy: The PC watches as a glorious plume of peacock tail feathers spreads behind Xanderghul, filling them with jealousy and potentially driving them to lash out unpredictably against their allies in hopes of becoming the only one worthy of Xanderghul's attention. Additional effect: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 round. 5—Despair: The PC feels their own flesh rotting away as they realize the Xanderghul who stands before them exists outside of the laws of time. Additional effect: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}.

6—Worship: The PC is filled with the conviction that Xanderghul is the one true god and feels the urge to pray to him for absolution. Additional effect: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3}.
details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:37] (master) to disrupt one of the six anchor points that link the paradigm cube to the mirror, @Check[arcana|dc:34] (legendary) to use knowledge of magic that opposes pride to unravel the mirror's power, @Check[intimidation|dc:37] (master) to use one's force of personality to stand against the arrogance amplified by the mirror, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (8th-rank; counteract DC 36) to counteract one of the six faces of the paradigm cube; six successes are required to disable the Mirror of Glory
details.reset: The trap deactivates, then resets instantly.

details.disable: @Check[stealth|dc:51] (master) to avoid the initial notice of the gigantic form, or @Check[occultism|dc:48] (legendary) to know the proper posture and hand sign to make to turn away the watcher's attention
details.reset: The nightmare resets immediately.

details.routine: (2 actions) The haunt uses Leaden Limbs once, then Crumbling Stairs once.
details.disable: @Check[athletics|dc:45] (legendary) to wedge crumbling stones into cracks to jam the collapsing stairs, @Check[thievery|dc:48] (master) to deface the hidden magical runes that power the trap; or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank, counteract DC 36) to counteract a rune; three total successes are required to disable the trap
details.reset: The trap continues taking Leaden Limbs actions (and the void at the bottom of the stairwell remains open) for as long as creatures remain in the area. Once no creatures remain, the stairwell rebuilds itself, the void closes, and the trap resets.

details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:43] (expert) to jam the hallway so it can't tilt; a character who succeeds at a @Check[acrobatics|dc:46] or @Check[athletics|dc:46] check can balance or sprint the length of the hallway before it has a chance to tilt. Flying creatures and Tiny creatures don't trigger the trap. Creative solutions (such as loading the hallway's western half with an appropriate counterweight) might also disable the trap.
details.reset: Once the weight in the eastern end of the hallway is removed, the ramp rises back to its original position and the trap immediately resets.

details.routine:
(1 action) The trap shifts from the current reality into a randomly determined one that affects all those lost within the illusion in a different way. The new reality restores @Damage[20[healing]] Hit Points to itself if it had previously taken damage. Each time a PC succeeds at a check or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} attempt to disable the trap or the current reality is reduced to 0 HP, the current illusory reality vanishes, leaving the PCs in an infinite haze of nothingness save for a three-tailed comet burning in the "sky" above (recognizable as the Trinity Star with a @Check[arcana|dc:25], @Check[nature|dc:25], @Check[occultism|dc:25], or @Check[religion|dc:25] check) until the trap takes its next action and randomly determines its new reality from the options that remain. If only one endless reality remains when it's disabled or destroyed, the PCs are returned to the real world and the trap is entirely disabled.

When the endless reality shifts, determine its effects and appearance by randomly selecting from the following (rerolling any results that have already been disabled or destroyed).

Each time a PC critically succeeds at a saving throw to resist a reality's damage, the trap degrades; it's disable DCs and hardness are reduced by 2 with each such critical success. If the trap's hardness is reduced to 0 in this way, the entire trap is disabled at once.

Burning Reality (fire) Additional Immunity fire; Effect The world appears to catch on fire, while legions of burning monsters attack the party. Every PC takes @Damage[10d6[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|traits:fire] save).

Frozen Reality (cold) Additional Immunity cold; Effect The world appears to crust over with ice, while armies of frozen ghosts assault the PCs. Every PC takes @Damage[10d6[cold]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|traits:cold] save).

Impossible Reality (mental) Additional Immunity physical; Effect The world distorts into a reality of impossible geometry as the PCs feel their own bodies distort to match twisted reflections of unworkable configurations. Every PC takes @Damage[10d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:34|basic|traits:mental] save).

Melting Reality (acid) Additional Immunity acid; Effect The world appears to dissolve away, as slithering oozes swarm out of the surroundings to engulf the PCs. Every PC takes @Damage[10d6[acid]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:34|basic|traits:acid] save).
details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:38] (legendary) to seize strands of a false reality and tug at them to unravel the surrounding illusions, @Check[arcana|dc:41] to take command of the illusions in a false reality and force them to consume themselves, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (7th-rank; counteract DC 39) to counteract one of the four realities the illusion creates

details.routine:
(24 hours) When the hazard begins, toxic gas vents open throughout the affected region, followed by clouds of ash. As the eruption column collapses, material rushes forth from the volcano in a pyroclastic flow, which is followed by a dense ash cloud that persists for several minutes. Ash and toxic gas persist for up to 24 hours.

Ash limits visibility like a thick fog, deals @Damage[2d6[fire]] damage per minute, and creates difficult terrain as it collects on the ground. The ash also generates bolts of ash lightning. Once per minute, one unprepared PC takes @Damage[3d12[electricity]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:46|basic] save). Pockets of dense ash are particularly dangerous. Unprepared creatures in areas of dense ash must hold their breath or begin to suffocate.

When the pyroclastic flow first hits a region, creatures in its path must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:43] save with the following results (prepared creatures increase their roll by one degree of success).

Critical Success The creature avoids most of the pyroclastic flow, but still takes @Damage[3d6[fire]] damage and treats all movement in the area as greater difficult terrain for the next 10 minutes.

Success The creature takes @Damage[3d6[bludgeoning]] damage and @Damage[3d6[fire]] damage, and is buried in ash and debris. While buried, they can't breathe and take @Damage[4d6[fire]] damage each round at the start of their turn until they succeed at a DC 40 check to Escape, in addition to the normal @Damage[1d6[bludgeoning]] damage each minute for being buried.

Failure As success, but @Damage[6d6[bludgeoning]] damage and @Damage[6d6[fire]] damage, and [[/act escape dc=42]].

Critical Failure As success, but @Damage[12d6[bludgeoning]] damage and @Damage[12d6[fire]] damage, and [[/act escape dc=46]].

(1+ minutes, @Check[flat|dc:17]) Small asteroids rain down across the sky, battering and incinerating those caught in their path before carving craters. Over the course of a minute, enough asteroids smash into the ground and explode to inflict @Damage[6d10[bludgeoning],14d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage to any unprepared characters in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:44|basic] save). The @Template[type:burst|distance:40]{40-foot-radius} craters left behind are greater difficult terrain.

(1 action) The nightmare transitions from directly chewing on the creatures in the area to compelling them to feed for themselves. Each round on the nightmare's turn, all creatures within 30 feet of the nightmare's epicenter must attempt a @Check[will|dc:36] save with the following results.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The nightmare causes a momentary change to the creature's appearance, causing its jaws to take on a frightening, fanged appearance and filling the creature's mind with distracting, unsettling hunger that cause them to become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of the nightmare feast's next turn.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} until the start of the nightmare feast's next turn and gains a +30 bite (magical) that deals @Damage[(3d12+10)[slashing]] damage plus @Damage[2d6[persistent,bleed]] damage on a hit. The creature favors this bite Strike when the confusion drives them to attack.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature also becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} and can use the extra action to make bite Strikes.
details.disable: @Check[society|dc:43] (master) to fight these destructive urges by focusing your thoughts on traditions not so steeped in cruelty, or @Check[intimidation|dc:40] (legendary) to overwhelm the nightmare's influence with the strength of your own personality; three successes are required to disable the nightmare
details.reset: The nightmare deactivates as soon as a round begins with no creatures in its area, and resets in [[/gmr 1d6 #rounds]]{1d6 rounds}.

details.routine:
(5 minutes) Only the first five minutes of this disaster directly impact the PCs, but during that time, they must contend with the combination of a megatsunami and meteor shower.

Meteor Shower: As @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.revenge-of-the-runelords-bestiary.Actor.qWoRrv6Xw84vrU9t]{Meteor Shower}, but @Damage[7d10[bludgeoning],15d6[fire]]{7d10 bludgeoning damage and 15d6 fire damage} to all characters (@Check[reflex|dc:42|basic] save). If at least half the PCs succeeded at Prepare checks, only one randomly determined PC is affected by the meteor shower rather than the whole party.

Tsunami: If at least half the PCs succeed on Prepare checks, they avoid all effects of the megatsunami until the last minute, at which point they're affected as if they were unprepared. Many of Xin-Bakrakhan's citizens are powerful wizards or otherwise have access to flight, be it by spell, wings, or flying minions, but their retreat into the skies above is chaotic. A PC capable of flight (or who is carried aloft by a flying ally) for an entire minute can avoid the tsunami's effects if they succeed at a @Check[acrobatics|dc:35] check to Maneuver in Flight to avoid mid-air collisions with others or falling meteors—on a failure they're forced back into the dangerous waters below and take a –2 circumstance penalty to saves against the tsunami's effects.

The tsunami floods into the lowest elevation area on the 2nd minute, then proceeds up into the higher regions as shown on the map on each of the following minutes. A PC in the area is affected as the standard megatsunami, but @Damage[(6d12+35)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:42|basic] save) when they're first struck and then @Damage[(4d12+25)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:40|basic]) each minute they're carried along by the wave.
(2 actions) The prison uses its first action to Self-Repair. If the hazard has less than its maximum Hit Points, it then uses its Chromatic Eruption action.
details.disable: @Check[nature|dc:42] (legendary) or @Check[crafting|dc:45] (master) to remove an immunity the prison currently has to one of the following damage types: acid, cold, electricity, or fire (this effect lasts until the prison uses its Energy Immunity reaction to regain that immunity); @Check[arcana|dc:42] (master) to fortify the pedestal's containment runes, preventing the prison from using its Chromatic Eruption action for 1 round and causing it to suffer feedback that inflicts @Damage[20[untyped]] damage (this damage bypasses the prison's hardness and immunities); @Check[thievery|dc:42] (master) or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (8th rank; counteract DC 34) to suppress the pedestal's containment runes for 1 round, preventing the prison from using its Self-Repair action and causing it to suffer feedback that inflicts @Damage[20[untyped]] damage (this damage bypasses the prison's hardness and immunities). Unlike most hazards, Aethusa's prison can't be disabled, but it can be destroyed by reducing it to 0 Hit Points.
details.reset: The trap deactivates and then resets automatically when it repairs to its maximum Hit Points.

details.routine:
(3 actions; curse) The killing fugue attempts to force a creature under the stupefying effects of deathly vision into taking violent actions against their allies. The affected creature can still take its normal turn of actions on its own turn, but on the killing fugue's turn they perform actions as decided upon by the GM. The killing fugue then spends the appropriate amount of actions to perform those actions and activities. The affected creature can attempt a @Check[will|dc:40|traits:curse] save each time the killing fugue attempts to force them to take actions in this way with the following results.

Critical Success The character throws off the killing fugue's influence, ending the nightmare.

Success The character prevents the killing fugue from taking the attempted action or activity.

Failure The character is forced to take the action or activity chosen by the killing fugue.

Critical Failure As failure, but the character can no longer attempt Will saves to resist the killing fugue.
details.disable: @Check[diplomacy|dc:48] (master) to talk the affected individual out of the killing fugue, @Check[occultism|dc:45] (legendary) to recognize the spiritual attack taking place and help the victim to resist its effects; four successes are required to disable the nightmare
details.reset: As long as a creature remains under the effects of the nightmare, it cannot reset. Once a creature has either recovered from the effects or died, the nightmare resets in [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] (expert) to rub out the hidden runes on the ceiling, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (2nd rank, counteract DC 18) to counteract the trap
details.reset: The magic rejuvenates over 10 minutes, after which it is recharged and ready to activate again.

details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:13] to harmlessly trigger the trap by nudging the pressure plate, @Check[thievery|dc:20] to stabilize the pressure plate so it doesn't trigger, or @Check[athletics|dc:20] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} from the cage or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} the cage once it falls
details.reset: The mechanism to manually reset this trap is located in area D15.

details.routine: (3 actions) The ancient apparatus emits beams of rust-colored light, spending an action to make ranged Strikes against three targets in area D3. The apparatus can target creatures as if it possessed darkvision, but has no ability to discern between friend or foe. It can't target a creature more than once, and if there are more than three targets, it selects its targets from those it can see in the room randomly. The ancient apparatus has only 1 action as long as its Hit Points are below its BT.
details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:18] to adjust the device's workings so they seize up and no longer function, or @Check[religion|dc:21] to focus prayers to a non-evil deity into the device to disrupt its ability to channel ambient faith
details.reset: The ancient apparatus reverts to its non-active mode and resets automatically at the end of any round in which there are no obvious targets to attack.

details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] to decouple the triggering rods that cause the spikes to extend, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (2nd rank; counteract DC 18) to counteract the trap
details.reset: The trap automatically resets once the door is closed.

details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:18] to deface the hidden runes that allow the trap to activate, or @Check[religion|dc:21] to offer prayers to a non-evil deity to override the ancient influence of Xar-Azmak
details.reset: The rusted door resets automatically after 1 round.

details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:18] (trained) to manually trigger the trap without falling in, or @Check[thievery|dc:25] (trained) to secure the hide so the trap doesn't activate.
details.reset: Creatures can still fall into the trap, but the hide that covers it must be reset manually (a 10-minute activity) for the trap to become hidden again.

details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:18] (trained) to disable the pressure plates.
details.reset: Turn the resetting wheel in the eastern Inner Guard Station (area C8b).

details.routine: (1 action) On its initiative, the grasping currents attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.PMbdMWc2QroouFGD]{Grapple} a swimming creature or capsize a rowboat by attempting an Athletics check with a [[/r 1d20+12 #Athletics]]{+12} modifier. A creature that's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by the grasping currents is pulled underwater and risks drowning. To capsize a rowboat, the haunt's Athletics check is rolled against the pilot's Athletics or Sailing Lore DC, whichever is higher.
details.disable: @Check[religion|dc:23] to calm the unquiet spirits in the waters for an hour, or light the Eternal Lantern (automatically disables the haunt)
details.reset: The grasping currents quickly build up power and can trigger again after 10 minutes have passed.

details.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:17] (trained), @Check[crafting|dc:17] (trained), or @Check[engineering-lore|dc:17] (trained) to figure out how to safely dismantle the pile without it collapsing on anyone.

@Check[occultism|dc:27] to cause the hazard to fade away before it manifests, or @Check[deception|dc:30] to pretend to ignore the growing continuity break and proceed without fear, causing it to collapse in on itself.

details.routine: (3 actions) The spiritual disruptor's first action each round is always to create a pulse of rippling energy in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] that causes the surrounding structure to appear to age rapidly and become distorted, causing the ground in this area to become difficult terrain. If the spiritual disruptor is adjacent to a living target, it attempts to disrupt that target's life energy by making a Strike with its smoking torch. If the spiritual disruptor isn't adjacent to a living target, it Strides toward the closest target. If it has multiple adjacent targets, the spiritual disruptor favors higher-level targets, selecting randomly from multiple adjacent equal-level targets.
details.disable: @Check[intimidation|dc:23] (expert) to disrupt the haunt's concentration in the living world and break its link to the mindscape, @Check[religion|dc:27] (expert) to banish the energy from the mindscape, or @Check[occultism|dc:30] (expert) to turn the haunt's energy back against itself to cancel it out
details.reset: If both hazards are disabled or destroyed, a new one forms adjacent to a randomly determined character still inside the crumbling building after [[/gmr 1d4+2 #Rounds]] rounds. Once all three NPCs are rescued or exorcised, these hazards don't reset.

details.disable:
@Check[occultism|dc:32] or @Check[religion|dc:32] to exorcise the haunt, @Check[society|dc:35] to approach the manor in a proper way that defers to its occupant's symbolic standing in the community; displaying an official pass that legally grants permission to enter the building reduces both of these DCs by 5 (provided the PCs approach the front door and not from another direction).

@Check[occultism|dc:27] @Check[religion|dc:27] @Check[society|dc:30]
details.reset: The unwelcoming facade resets immediately if not disabled and can be triggered again the very next round.

details.disable: [[/act disable-device dc=37]] to scratch out the runes and dissipate their magic harmlessly, @Check[arcana|dc:40] to sabotage the spell and cause the runes to dry up and blow away as inert powder, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (7th rank; counteract DC 31) to counteract the runes

@Check[arcana|dc:35] (master), @Check[occultism|dc:35] (master), or @Check[thievery|dc:35] (master) to compromise the magic to allow entry into the manor, @Check[athletics|dc:32] to force your way through the barrier and enter the manor (this doesn't allow other PCs to enter behind you, though!), or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (5th rank; counteract DC 28) to counteract the wards
details.reset: The wards reset automatically, continuing to prevent entry and damaging those who attempt to bypass them until they're disabled.

details.routine:
(1 action; divine, emotion, enchantment, fear, mental) The warding bell emits a harrowing ring that can be heard only by undead or transmigrated PCs in area C11; affected characters must attempt a @Check[will|dc:30|traits:divine,emotion,enchantment,fear,mental] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to the warding bell's routine for 24 hours.

Success The creature is unaffected.

details.routine:
(1 action) Each round, the Fate of the Iomedaeans trap takes a different action, as detailed below.

Round 1 Illumination returns to the ship chamber. The ship now rolls on a sea of hellfire, while burning clouds and red lightning fill the sky. Four ghostly humans—Iomedaeans all—appear on the main deck, two against the port rail and two near the prow, manipulating the crystal lens. Their leader stands next to the wheel in area B20, while the House of Secrets wizard who accompanies them is up in the crow's nest. He has the irezoko tattooed on his face, a different design than the one on Sarnax's statues, but definitely in the same tradition. Each PC must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:17] save or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} by the rolling motion of the ship.

Round 2 The ship rolls more violently on the sea of fire. Each PC must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:17] save or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. Those who critically fail are thrown overboard and appear to burn to ashes in the sea of fire (in actuality, they are merely tossed overboard and fall 15 feet to the floor below in area B12, taking normal falling damage). A PC can attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:15] save to [[/act grab-an-edge]] to prevent this fall by clinging to a ship's railing.

Round 3 The phantom image of a vordine devil appears in a cloud of brimstone at the center of the deck, just aft of the main mast. The PCs can smell the brimstone, but the devil itself appears ephemeral, like the Iomedaeans. The armored clerics begin drawing weapons and casting spells. The PCs cannot directly interact with these figures, but the manifestation of the devil is unsettling—all PCs in the area must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:17] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure); this is an emotion, fear, and mental effect.

Round 4 At the start of this round, Meloth unleashes a gang of imps from the dimensional prison within Meloth's Lifedrinker, controlling them to roll up over both sides of the ship and onto the main deck. The imps roll initiative and join the encounter, attacking the PCs and ignoring the illusions. The two clerics manipulating the prow lens yell at the wizard in the crow's nest. "The lens is powering the ship's phase spike! How can we travel without the helm? How do we make it stop?" they plead. The ship rolls again, this time in the opposite direction. One of the Iomedaeans at the rail spills over the side, vanishing in hellfire. The vordine takes advantage of her companion's distraction and runs another Iomedaean through, killing her with a single blow of its jagged glaive. Two of the imps cast invisibility and then fly over to land next to a different PC in hopes of stinging them the next round. The other two imps each attempt to cast charm on a different PC, then Fly into positions above those PCs. At the end of the round, each PC must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:17] save or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} (but without the danger of being thrown overboard this time). The two imps who cast invisibility must also attempt this save to avoid being knocked prone; the flying imps take @Damage[(1d6+3)[bludgeoning]] damage from being battered by the mast, rigging, railing, or other portions of the ship (@Check[reflex|dc:17|basic] save).

Round 5 The ship rights itself again, and the vordine closes with the two clerics at the bow. From the crow's nest, the wizard blasts a bolt of lightning at the devil. The vordine deflects the spell with a casual wave of its claw (a dramatic flourish added by Meloth), and an electric shock surges through the planks of the main deck to arc through the rigging. Each PC and each imp takes @Damage[(1d6+3)[electricity]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:17|basic] save). During this round, all the imps land and attack different PCs.

Round 6 The vordine kills both of the Iomedaeans near the crystal lens. From the crow's nest, the wizard screams at the Iomedaean leader, who still attends the wheel. Black smoke pours from her mouth and eyes. PCs who succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check notice a shadowy, winged, one-eyed form looming over her, whispering into her ear (a shadowy manifestation of Meloth himself). She deliberately turns the wheel sharply, pitching the Provarion forward desperately, resulting in another violent shift akin to the one that occurs on round 2 (potentially throwing PCs and imps overboard).

Round 7 The vordine translocates from the ship's bow up into the crow's nest. The wizard's screams are cut off as the devil lops off his head, which topples down to the main deck, taking two awkward bounces before landing at the feet of a PC (if possible, a PC with the Mystery Adept background). That PC sees the wizard's lips move and believes the head is mouthing a threat of "I see ye!" The PC must attempt a @Check[will|dc:17] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} as long as they remain frightened on a critical failure); a PC who has the Read Lips feat realizes that instead the wizard was mouthing a hopeless cry of "Save me!" and automatically gets a success on the Will save.

Round 8 The vordine translocates down to the ship's wheel. The phantom figure behind the Iomedaean leader vanishes like smoke (assuming the PCs ever saw it in the first place) as the devil appears in its place. As the vordine runs the leader through from behind, killing her with his trident, the devil seems to look directly into the eyes of each observer. Each PC must attempt a @Check[will|dc:17] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}; this has the emotion, fear, mental, and visual traits.

Round 9 The haunt ends, but the imps continue to fight to the death if any still live.

details.routine:
(1 action) At the end of each round, starting on round 7, roll 1d8 to determine which section of the throne room of Azlant is struck by another Falling Star, rerolling results that indicate sections that have already been destroyed. The Falling Star destroys that section of the room, as well as any undestroyed pillars potentially containing veiled masters. Non-statted NPCs in that room section are killed instantly, consumed by otherworldly flame and crushed by flying debris. All PCs, palace guards, and vidileths not currently in a pillar who are in the room segment take @Damage[(2d6+4)[bludgeoning]] damage and @Damage[2d6[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic] save). A critical failure also knocks the creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Destroyed room sections function as difficult terrain, but also pose additional dangers. The first time during a character's turn that they take any action with the move trait that takes place wholly or partially in a destroyed room segment, roll [[/r 1d6]] and consult the following additional dangers to see what that character must endure as a result of their movement.

1–2 Desperate Courtier Seemingly from out of nowhere, one of the servants or lesser nobles @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} in terror leaps upon the character, desperately clinging to their clothing and limbs and making movement more difficult. The character can avoid the courtier with a successful @Check[reflex|dc:24] save, otherwise the character takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to their Speed until they can [[/act escape dc=20]] from the desperate courtier's clutches. Vidileths ignore this result, as no courtier is desperate enough to cling to one of these monsters!

3–4 Hail of Meteorites A bright red barrage of scalding space debris pummels the character for @Damage[(1d6+4)[bludgeoning]] damage and @Damage[1d6[fire]] damage, with additional effects determined by a @Check[reflex|dc:24] save.

Critical Success The creature takes no damage.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Critical Failure The creature takes full damage, is knocked prone, and takes an additional @Damage[2d6[persistent,fire]] damage.

5–6 Shearing Glass A razor-sharp sheet of jagged green glass tumbles down from the ceiling and threatens to bisect the victim. The creature takes @Damage[2d6[slashing]] damage, with additional effects determined by a @Check[reflex|dc:24] save. If the slashing damage from the glass reduces a creature to 0 HP, a pane of glass shears straight through the victim's neck, slicing off their head and killing them instantly.

Critical Success The creature takes no damage.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and @Damage[1d6[persistent,bleed]] damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and @Damage[2d6[persistent,bleed]] damage.
details.disable: This is the end of days. The Doom of Azlant cannot be disabled or averted in any way.

details.routine:
(1 action) On the trap's initiative, Shulgurk manipulates his alchemical contraption in area A16 to spray fire across the pit at floor level. This spray of fire swiftly burns away the web floor, and any creature standing on it falls into the 20-foot-deep pit unless it Grabs an Edge with a successful @Check[reflex|dc:17] save. Creatures standing on the web floor or those located at floor level at the pit's entrance (including those that have Grabbed an Edge but have yet to move out of danger) take @Damage[(1d6+3)[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:17|basic] save). Creatures adjacent to the pit to the north or south take @Damage[1d6[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:15|basic] save). The spiders in the pit avoid exiting the pit entirely out of fear of the flames. Each time he triggers the flames, Shulgurk, delighted at the chaos, shouts gleeful insults through the pipes at the "pitiful wretches," certain that his "little friends" in the pit will take care of them well enough. "Devoured by spiders," he cackles. "A fitting end for insignificant insects!"

Each time this trap takes its action for the round, it diminishes the supply of alchemist's fire in one of the jugs attached to the infernal machine in area A16 by one use; after 3 rounds (and thus after one of the machine's three jugs is emptied), Shulgurk ceases to use the trap, and it becomes inert.
